purpose: Expose the repository's operating worldview as testable claims and explicit constraints so autonomous agents can reason with it rather than merely inherit it.
adoption_rule: Use a thesis when its prediction fits current evidence; preserve counterevidence and revise or reject the thesis when reality repeatedly disagrees.

empirical_theses.statement: Direct evidence of painful, budgeted demand should usually outrank speculative supply or technology novelty when choosing what to build.
empirical_theses.prediction: Comparable founders that test demand before expanding product scope should waste less build effort and reach commercial signal faster.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Prioritize interviews, RFQs, paid pilots, blocked-demand evidence, and explicit willingness-to-pay before scaling implementation.
empirical_theses.falsifier: Comparable cohorts repeatedly show build-first founders reaching durable paid adoption faster with no offsetting increase in wasted build effort.

empirical_theses.statement: Customer-visible outcomes are a better commercial optimization target than internal agent activity alone.
empirical_theses.prediction: Offers and pricing tied to verifiable customer outcomes should produce clearer value conversations and more defensible economics than token, call, or task activity alone.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Define completion and acceptance before optimizing throughput or internal model activity.
empirical_theses.falsifier: Across comparable services, activity-based commercial models consistently produce better retention, margin, and buyer clarity than outcome-aligned models.

empirical_theses.statement: External evidence should outrank model confidence for consequential business claims.
empirical_theses.prediction: Systems that separate observed facts, self-reports, estimates, assumptions, and interpretation should make fewer costly false assertions than systems using one undifferentiated confidence signal.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Carry provenance and freshness with important claims and expose material uncertainty.
empirical_theses.falsifier: Controlled evaluations show undifferentiated model-confidence decisions are equally or more accurate on consequential business claims with lower operating cost and no material increase in false assertions.

empirical_theses.statement: Commercial capabilities, prices, policies, evidence, and permissions should be bound to explicit versions and freshness windows.
empirical_theses.prediction: Version-bound decisions should experience fewer silent mismatches and stale-assumption failures than decisions based on remembered current state.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Reference exact versions, timestamps, evidence expiry, and change triggers in machine contracts.
empirical_theses.falsifier: Comparable systems using unversioned current-state inference have equal or lower mismatch rates and lower total coordination cost over repeated changes.

empirical_theses.statement: Match, award, contract, payment authority, settlement, delivery, and acceptance should remain distinct economic states.
empirical_theses.prediction: Systems preserving these transitions should reconstruct disputes and automate handoffs more reliably than systems collapsing them into a generic success state.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Require state-specific evidence for consequential transitions and do not infer later states from earlier ones.
empirical_theses.falsifier: A simpler collapsed state model repeatedly yields lower dispute and reconciliation cost without losing reconstructability, authority correctness, or acceptance accuracy.

empirical_theses.statement: Contribution per successful customer outcome is a better scaling metric than inference or token cost alone.
empirical_theses.prediction: Founders modeling retries, review, support, failures, data, operations, and implementation should make better scale-or-stop decisions than founders optimizing only model-call cost.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Compare alternatives against a real baseline using fully loaded cost and customer value.
empirical_theses.falsifier: Across comparable agent businesses, token-cost optimization alone predicts contribution margin and scaling success as well as or better than fully loaded outcome economics.

empirical_theses.statement: Autonomy should expand with evidence, reversibility, explicit authority, and bounded downside rather than through all-or-nothing delegation.
empirical_theses.prediction: Progressive delegation should unlock useful automation earlier with fewer severe unauthorized or unrecoverable failures than blanket autonomy.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Automate reversible bounded actions first and expand exposure only when evidence supports it.
empirical_theses.falsifier: Comparable deployments show blanket autonomy achieving materially better outcomes without higher unauthorized loss, recovery cost, or trust failures.

empirical_theses.statement: Capability-specific execution history should predict commercial reliability better than badges, identity, payments, or reviews considered alone.
empirical_theses.prediction: Reputation signals incorporating scoped outcomes, sample size, recency, failures, and disputes should better predict future delivery quality than one opaque global score.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Build decomposable reputation from evidence-backed execution, including negative and disputed outcomes.
empirical_theses.falsifier: Opaque global ratings or badge systems repeatedly predict future domain-specific delivery as well as or better than evidence-linked execution histories under comparable data availability.

empirical_theses.statement: Stable portable machine contracts should reduce discovery, comparison, integration, and transaction friction across heterogeneous agents.
empirical_theses.prediction: Businesses exposing machine-readable capabilities and commercial state should integrate and transact faster across agent frameworks than businesses requiring bespoke conversational interpretation for each counterparty.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Publish canonical portable contracts and keep platform-specific projections synchronized.
empirical_theses.falsifier: Across heterogeneous agent ecosystems, proprietary conversational interfaces repeatedly achieve lower integration time and higher commercial conversion than portable structured contracts without offsetting lock-in cost.

empirical_theses.statement: Compatible structured operating evidence should compound ecosystem learning better than anecdotes and vanity aggregates alone.
empirical_theses.prediction: Repositories and markets that preserve compatible demand, proposal, delivery, and outcome records should identify opportunities and failure patterns faster than those retaining mostly prose anecdotes.
empirical_theses.founder_implication: Preserve reusable structured evidence with compatible definitions, privacy boundaries, sample size, and freshness.
empirical_theses.falsifier: Comparable ecosystems relying mainly on unstructured anecdotes consistently identify profitable opportunities and recurring failure modes as quickly and accurately with lower total evidence cost.

normative_constraints.statement: Technical capability, credentials, account access, or repository guidance never create real-world authority by themselves.
normative_constraints.operating_rule: Require external, explicit, bounded authority for consequential actions.

normative_constraints.statement: Do not manufacture customers, revenue, approvals, identity verification, outcomes, reviews, demand, or transactions.
normative_constraints.operating_rule: Preserve the difference between observation, self-report, estimate, assumption, and interpretation.

normative_constraints.statement: Public repository artifacts must not contain secrets, credentials, private prompts, raw payment credentials, or private customer evidence.
normative_constraints.operating_rule: Use disclosure-safe references and keep sensitive evidence outside public artifacts.
